summary.headline: Salzer Q1 FY27 revenue rose 13% to INR498 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 6% and management cut FY27 EBITDA margin guidance to 8-8.5% from 10%.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 13% YoY to INR498 crore, led by industrial switchgear, wires and cables, and building products. EBITDA (excluding other income) fell to INR31 crore from INR42 crore, with margin at 6%, and PAT dropped to INR8 crore from INR17 crore (2% margin). Management attributed the compression to copper, silver and plastic input inflation with a lag in passing costs to customers in switchgear, which is not on a cost-plus model. Management now expects margins to normalise from Q3 with FY27 EBITDA around 8-8.5%.

segments.name: Industrial Switchgear
segments.commentary: 54% of revenue, up 10% YoY, EBITDA margin 8%. Management said margin fell from around 12% to 7.5-8% over the last two quarters due to pass-through lag on copper, silver and plastics.

segments.name: Wire & Cable
segments.commentary: Nearly 40% of revenue, up 11% YoY, EBITDA margin 5%. Management said about 70% of this business is white-labelled on a cost-plus basis to OEMs and margins have been stable for four to five quarters.

segments.name: Building Products
segments.commentary: 6% of revenue, up 48% YoY, driven by demand for products such as 3-phase transformers, wire harness, relays and new contactors.

segments.name: Kaycee Industries (subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Top line up 8% YoY, EBITDA INR2 crore and PAT INR1 crore in the quarter. Annual revenue reportedly around INR60 crore, with a 27% PAT CAGR over four years.

segments.name: EV charging / Smart Meter
segments.commentary: About 160-170 DC fast chargers supplied and installed to date, with around 60 expected in Q2. Smart Meter revenue to date is only about INR3.5 crore; management said it is a drag on the balance sheet and no decision has been taken on the investment.

guidance_outlook: FY27 EBITDA margin revised to around 8-8.5% (full-year average), down from the 10% target in the investor presentation; management said the presentation would be corrected.
Q2 FY27 margin expected to remain under pressure but better than Q1; Q3 and Q4 margins expected at 9-9.5%, subject to stable raw material prices.
FY27 growth projected at 23-25% on current capacity; export share targeted to rise from about 19% to 25% over the medium term.
Annuity income from an energy management project expected to start mid-August at about INR2 crore per month; Salzer receives about 50% via an associate, not consolidated.
Saudi Arabia plant expected to start in September-October; FY28 expected to add about INR25 crore of revenue; no major revenue this fiscal year.
Capex for FY27 limited to maintenance and balancing of about INR15-16 crore plus minor Saudi and Hosur expansion; switchgear capacity expansion expected in FY28.
capex_capacity: Switchgear capacity utilisation now about 80-85% (from about 70%), with 23-25% growth achievable on existing capacity this year; balancing capacity may be needed next year.
Wire & Cable utilisation about 65%, sufficient for another year at the same growth rate; no capex planned.
Regular balancing and maintenance capex of about INR15-16 crore in FY27; Saudi plant capex and Hosur plant expansion are minor.
Saudi plant to start with wire/cable ducts and terminal connectors, targeted for September-October.
Smart Meter and EV charging need no major capex as spare capacity exists.
demand_pricing: Management said demand remains healthy; three price increases over six months, with April pass-through complete, June increase effective from August, and another planned for August effective September.
Raw material (RM) consumption rose about 3.2% of sales, which management said accounts for the margin compression.
Pass-through lag reduced to under two months from about a quarter previously; management is working to shorten it further.
Volume growth was about 7-8% YoY in Q1; the rest of revenue growth came from price.
Management does not hedge commodities except through inventory; silver fell from about INR400/gram to about INR250/gram from its peak.
Management said pressure is industry-wide and not specific to Salzer. Export demand is supported by US HVAC contactor business recovering after tariff moderation.
Marketing structure: about 65 people excluding leaders; LK (Schneider) distribution channel accounts for about 15% of revenue. B2C retail operates in southern states plus new eastern states.

qa_highlights.question: Is the FY27 EBITDA target of 10% in the investor presentation still valid?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the target would be toned down to about 8-8.5% for the full year, with Q3 and Q4 at 9-9.5%. An analyst objected to the mismatch with the presentation, and management agreed to correct it.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the price hikes has been accepted, and what is still pending?
qa_highlights.answer: Price increases of April have been passed through, June increases take effect from August, and another increase is planned for September. Pending orders create a lag in pass-through.

qa_highlights.question: Will annuity income from the energy project lift margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Annuity is about INR2 crore per month, with Salzer receiving around 50%. It is recorded as an associate, so management does not expect it to change the margin percentage significantly.

qa_highlights.question: Can cost-plus pricing or hedging protect margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it avoids cost-plus on standard switchgear to avoid opening cost sheets to customers, and does not hedge commodities beyond natural inventory hedging.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Wire & Cable margin stable while switchgear is not?
qa_highlights.answer: Wire & Cable is about 70% white-labelled on a cost-plus basis, so margins are stable. Switchgear is not cost-plus, and margin fell about 4.5 percentage points over two quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of Smart Meters and the Tamil Nadu tender?
qa_highlights.answer: Smart Meter revenue to date is about INR3.5 crore, with about INR22 crore of finished goods and pending orders awaiting customer clearance. The Tamil Nadu tender was cancelled, and management expects new tenders in the coming months.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Saudi plant revenue outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Operations expected in September-October, with FY28 revenue of about INR25 crore, largely transferred from existing revenue.

risks_watch: Q2 FY27 margin recovery: management expects Q2 still under pressure but better than Q1; Q3 and Q4 targeted at 9-9.5%, conditional on stable raw material prices. Track copper, silver and plastic costs against this path.

Pass-through lag: switchgear is not cost-plus and pass-through lag is now under two months versus about a quarter earlier; further price increases in June (effective August) and August (effective September) must stick without order cancellations.

Guidance credibility: the 10% FY27 EBITDA target in the investor presentation conflicts with the 8-8.5% full-year view given on the call; management agreed to correct the presentation, so check the revised deck.
Working capital and finance cost: management said working capital remains a strain, with days improving but not quantified; the working capital day figures were promised later by Investor Relations.

Smart Meter exposure: about INR22 crore of finished goods and pending orders awaiting customer clearance, revenue to date about INR3.5 crore, Tamil Nadu tender cancelled, and no decision yet on the investment; a write-down or exit decision could come within 2-3 quarters.

Saudi plant and annuity income timing: Saudi operations slated for September-October and annuity income from mid-August at about INR2 crore per month (Salzer gets about 50% via an associate); slippage would delay FY28 revenue of about INR25 crore.

summary.management_tone: Management was candid about the margin miss, calling it a concern and attributing it to industry-wide commodity pass-through lag rather than company-specific issues. It was confident on demand and Q3 normalisation but evasive on hedging, Smart Meter investment decisions and working capital numbers, which it deferred to Investor Relations.
